pr_title: Bluetooth: Controller: Add Kconfig for minimal time reservation
pr_body:
Add Kconfig to use minimal time reservation for auxiliary
and sync PDU reception. A peer device could be scheduling
multiple advertising sets in a short duration with small
PDUs hence using the minimal time reservation would avoid
skipping closely scheduled reception of multiple auxiliary
PDUs.

Add implementation in Periodic Sync LLL abort to use near
fair scheduling to ensure overlapping multiple Periodic
Sync set each get to use the radio and not lead to Sync
Loss.

The implementation is used when overlap in radio event
happens in unreserved time space of the event. An abort
count is maintain in each Periodic Sync instance and is
used to decide whether the current event or the next
event is to be aborted when they overlap.

Fixes #49465.

Signed-off-by: Vinayak Kariappa Chettimada <vich@nordicsemi.no>

issue_context.title: Bluetooth: Controller: Periodic adv. sync. degraded performance on latest main branch
issue_context.body:
**Describe the bug**
In the below table it can be seen that current main branch of Zephyr is not working as we expect. We expect the performance to be as with nRF Connect 2.0 or **_better_**.
This is tested with https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/pull/49429 code, which is a small addition to the main branch as of today.
15 Tags nRF Connect 2.0             |  15 Tags Zephyr main
:-------------------------:|:-------------------------:
![ncs_2-0-15-tags](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/4318648/186423916-9a429f93-b26f-4bd7-b1f9-c6322521b24d.PNG)             |  ![zephyr-main-15-tags](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/4318648/186423943-60f68510-5bcb-4de0-a95a-e805a295a640.PNG)
20 Tags nRF Connect 2.0             |  20 Tags Zephyr main
![ncs_2-0-20-tags](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/4318648/186424080-8e180c65-87a3-4f8b-be5f-d5e04bc55aee.PNG)             |  ![zephyr-main-20-tags](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/4318648/186424099-759c0cef-fa61-4f51-8c2f-8802108bab44.PNG)

One difference I can see in the logs are that for Zephyr main branch I get many prints as below.
That is sync_term callback but the le address is invalid (garbage). 
```
PER_ADV_SYNC[4]: [DEVICE]: 00:D9:AC:00:00:00 (public-id) sync terminated reason: 62
[00:00:17.917,205] <err> u_df_scan: Got sync_term from none queued tag!
```

Please also mention any information which could help others to understand
the problem you're facing:
 - What target platform are you using? - Zephyr SDK and NRF52833
 - Is this a regression? - Bisect is in progress...

**To Reproduce**
Build below application based on the `direction_finding_connectionless_rx` sample (the application does not enable CTE sampling by default but can still reproduce the issue).
[aoa_receiver_multiple_configureable.zip](https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/files/9416562/aoa_receiver_multiple_configureable.zip)

There are some options in the top of the main.c file, default is using periodic adv. list. which is also from where the images above are taken using.

NOTE if you build for other commits than https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/pull/49429 the line `CONFIG_BT_CTLR_SYNC_PERIODIC_SKIP_ON_SCAN_AUX=y` needs to be commented out in prj.conf

Have about 10 tags sending periodic advertisements (I used about 50ms interval and about 30 bytes per. adv. data payload, this is probably not needed) for example use `direction_finding_connectionless_tx` sample, the `periodic_adv` should also work, but I have not tried.

**Expected behavior**
Equal behaviour or better in Zephyr main branch compared to Zephyr version used in nRF Connect 2.0

**Impact**
Degraded performance when tracking many tags in an application

**Logs and console output**
[ncs_2-0-20-tags.log](https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/files/9416248/ncs_2-0-log-20-tags.log)
[ncs-2-0-15-tags.log](https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/files/9416249/ncs-2-0-15-tags.log)
[zephyr-main-15-tags.log](https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/files/9416250/zephyr-main-15-tags.log)
[zephyr-main-20-tags.log](https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/files/9416251/zephyr-main-20-tags.log)

**Environment (please complete the following information):**
 - OS: Windows
 - Toolchain: Zephyr SDK
 - Commit SHA or Version used: Used the code as in https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/pull/49429

@jakkra I have tested 5 tags synchronized under simulation under two conditions; one, all 5 tags have overlapping periodic advertising and all the 5 tags got synchronized; two, 5 tags with a progressive offset over time and only 4 tags got synchronized. But in both cases I was using duplicate filtering, stopping and starting scanning,  saw no issues, and periodic_sync device discovered extended advertising all along (except the one that was not synchronized). In the second case 5th tag was not discovered and this is possible if the auxiliary PDU of the 5th was overlapping any of the periodic advertising sync constantly. Keeping the periodic interval at 10 ms and extended advertising at a multiple of 10 ms would cause constant overlap between extended advertising event and periodic advertising event.

_Extended Advertising auxiliary PDU transmissions are implemented as periodic events_, a design choice to support non-overlapping multiple Extended and Periodic sets as a broadcaster. This means multiple broadcaster devices with same extended advertising interval will have overlapping auxiliary PDUs and make it difficult for a Periodic Sync device in discovering these overlapping broadcasters.

My testing yesterday was under simulation in BabbleSim. But on a target I suspect the overlapping may be too much for CPU processing between overlapping events. Something that was discovered during conformance testing of mixed multiple sets of extended advertising, periodic advertising synchronization and on multiple PHYs.

On target, the temporary solution was https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/commit/a40a403a0dfc8fdf573b4ba436d51d84d68a8bd1 

There is room for improvement in how ticker module schedules closely expiring timeouts. Currently, a minimum of 3 ticks is used between consecutive ticker expiry callbacks implemented by:
https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/blob/be7173a49054e34ee02d1e7ec713aabb6acc89a7/subsys/bluetooth/controller/ticker/ticker.c#L2405-L2429

Use of minimal time reservation causes many just-in-time scheduling decisions being taken and consecutive ticker expiry that consume time leading to the winning event being delayed to an amount that it cancels itself not being able to meet the hard real-time instant required to start the radio event.

To keep the just-in-time scheduling mitigation at O(1), i.e. scheduling decision take only based on time reservation, we have to not use the minimal time reservations, need #49579:

```
CONFIG_BT_CTLR_ADVANCED_FEATURES=y
CONFIG_BT_CTLR_SCAN_AUX_SYNC_RESERVE_MIN=n
```

Please let me know if the above Kconfig setting is acceptable by your application.
